rederivations.b1_answer: THE BYTE-COMPARE RECEIVES key[3] — the FOURTH DWORD of the 4-DWORD key tuple, i.e. the value 745BF0 itself received as ITS first stack argument ([ESP+0x4] @00745bf0). NOT key[1]: the constant 4 lands in S4 and acts as the scan's additive base (ESI=4), which (a) makes every compared byte sit at [cursor+4] — the tag byte at entry offset +4 of each 8-byte entry — and (b) leaves the returned cursor an ABSOLUTE ENTRY POINTER, consistent with the caller's success-path deref MOV EAX,[EAX] @00745c35 (P07 window) reading the payload DWORD at entry+0. key[0]/key[2] land in S3/S5 and are dead in the callee (their in-window provenance: reads of 745BF0's own never-written local block — stale/caller-leftover values, harmless because never consumed).
rederivations.consistency_with_prior_qc: the P07_QC_R1 review (reviews/P07_QC_R1/QC_REPORT.md) independently recorded the same mapping ('callee 745A70 receives [this+4], [this+8], &arg1 and the key by value; 4-DWORD key (const 4 at +0x4)') — QC re-derivation agrees slot-for-slot.
consequences: P10-5 CONFIRMED with slot precision: the composite key is NOT consumed as a composite; exactly one tuple DWORD (key[3]) reaches the compare, and only its low byte can match (0..255);

P10-8/B4 RESOLVED by the authorized re-check: S4 = 4 (nonzero) and the cursor is an absolute entry pointer (caller derefs the raw return); the '+4' is a fixed tag-offset inside the 8-byte entry, not a base-pointer/offset duality;
id2/class-20006 falsifier now slot-exact: if 745BF0's caller ever feeds 20006 into 745BF0's ARG1, then key[3]=S6=20006 > 255 -> guaranteed always-fail -> JZ 0x00745c40 fail exit taken;
remaining edges unchanged: B2 (array populator — still no VA in any admitted window) and the value semantics of 745BF0's ARG1 (caller-of-745BF0 window, never admitted).
rederivations.verdict: B1 SETTLED: key[3] (the tuple slot written at 00745c20 from 745BF0's ARG1) reaches the byte-compare; constant 4 (key[1]) reaches the base term; key[0]/key[2] dead
